source.limitation: Complete only for the authenticated UI feed at research time. LinkedIn may withhold, remove, or otherwise make historical records inaccessible.

global_search.scope: Visible authenticated LinkedIn content-search results; not a claim of exhaustive global-search coverage.
global_search.decision_policy: Posts are discovery leads. Only independently inspectable primary sources can create an implementation candidate.

findings.project_gap: Answer and citation evaluation existed, but route selection, graph-edge evidence, and tool efficiency were not scored as one trace.

findings.topic: Agentic graph retrieval and structural rewards
findings.adopted: Observable multi-step graph retrieval and structural evaluation.
findings.deferred: RL training and learned reward optimization until expert-labelled trajectories exist.

findings.reason: Preliminary work; current query planner, graph traversal, and agentic fallback already cover the immediate operational need.

findings.adopted: Golden-set schema now accepts expected retrieval surfaces, evidence IDs, graph edges, and tool budgets.
findings.deferred: Importing the specialized K-12 dataset as a general production benchmark.

findings.project_evidence: Ontology proposals, migration, SHACL mutation gates, versioning, review, semantic export, and MCP are already native capabilities.

findings.reason: Potentially useful for source stance, but confidence, contradictions, named provenance, and claim evidence already cover most current use cases.
Illustrative validation does not justify migrating the explicit provenance-bound production schema.
Claims are primarily self-benchmarked; backend adoption requires independent correctness and operations evidence.

findings.project_evidence: The platform already exposes API, UI/MCP surfaces, ingestion, identity resolution, ontology, intelligence artifacts, temporal/geographic expansion, JSON-LD tables, evaluation, and deployment assets.
Claims and graph elements carry source provenance; semantic interchange supports RDF/JSON-LD and provenance-aware controlled graphs.
Context Graph records decisions, episodes, observations, tool calls, policy versions, evidence, and replayable traces.

findings.topic: GraphRAG ranking skepticism and third-hop expansion risk
findings.project_evidence: Depth is bounded, multi-hop candidates are capped and semantically blended, graph weight is conservative, and retrieval changes are evaluation-gated.

findings.topic: Explicit document-link topology for multi-hop retrieval
findings.reason: Document hyperlink structure improved multi-hop web QA in the cited work. The platform has no explicit ingestion of HTML or SharePoint document-to-document links.
findings.gate: Limit to link-bearing sources, preserve tenant/access/provenance metadata on LINKS_TO edges, and release only if a link-dependent golden set improves without harming ordinary document retrieval.

findings.topic: Two-stage typed extraction and compact domain-adapted extractor
findings.project_evidence: GraphWriter applies tenant-scoped alias resolution and embedding deduplication; EntitySplitter and GraphEvaluator address over-merges and graph quality; incremental community controls support ongoing corpus change.
findings.deferred: Benchmark the reported compact extraction model against the configured providers before changing any production model default.
